decision.title: XDM values are immutable and reference counted
decision.summary: XDM values are immutable with reference counts on heap cells in an sxml_item_heap and small values inline; owned outputs are released exactly once, and node items retain their tree.

body.p: (task 0.7). Considered: an arena per evaluation (simple, but garbage grows without bound in long loops and folds, and values that escape the evaluation, such as results, global variables, XSLT keys and cached documents, need another mechanism), tracing garbage collection (needs root scanning of C stacks), and reference counting. Chosen: immutable values with reference counts on heap cells, small values inline. XDM values cannot form cycles (built bottom-up, never changed; closures capture values), so counting reclaims everything. Rules: outputs of make/put/append/... are owned (+1) and released exactly once; get/describe outputs are borrowed; inputs are borrowed and functions that store an input retain it themselves. Retain and release are no-ops on inline values and on immortal cells (static data, counts that would overflow). Cells live in an sxml_item_heap and record their heap, so sxml_item_release(item) needs no other argument. sxml_item_heap_read_counts reports live cells, so every test can check for leaks (with 's counting allocator for failure paths). Trees are counted too: node items retain their tree.
